correctness.rationale: For each bipartite edge, all t+1 natural neighbors depend on the opposite part at t, separating the two alternating vertex-time strands. One shift from empty initial natural state equates their optimum saturation costs; a fully naturally positive target forces saturation of each strand, and a saturated side propagates naturally after zero-cost updates. On K_{a,b}, natural successor counts are f(v),g(u) regardless of identities, giving exact nonnegative Dijkstra transition weights v-g(u),u-f(v) and optimum twice the minimum distance to a saturated side. Initial source arcs u correctly charge time-0 targeting. Uniform case requires min(alpha,beta) direct activations before first natural event or saturation.

The biclique specialization strictly generalizes prior star and restricted majority biclique examples.
